I am old now, 82 years, and my body is tired. This small piece of land, just a little more than one-tenth of a hectare, I plant with beans mixed together with my maize as I have always done. I have no money for fertilizer from the shop, and beans do not need it much anyway — they feed the soil themselves. I keep seeds from last year's harvest, as my mother did, and I work slowly with my own hands. Sometimes a grandchild helps me weed when the rains come hard.
